title: Frequency-autoregressive image generation: what have we learned?
occasion: Lab discussion with Prof. Shai Avidan

slides.title: Frequency-AR image generation: what have we learned?
slides.notes:
Purpose: a one-slide state of the project.
Claim: on FFHQ-64, our frequency-autoregressive model A1 (11.1M parameters) reaches FID-50K 9.46 with recall 0.413 using a validated UniPC schedule of 46 serial network evaluations. Our own DCTdiff port R0 (44.2M) with the same solver family reaches 8.68 / 0.440 at 15 evaluations. Both are measured with the same q90 reference and EDM Inception evaluator on 50k samples.
What is genuinely promising: 4x fewer parameters at ~1.09x the FID; on FFHQ the causal model beats its own joint control (slide 7).
What is weak: serial depth (46 vs 15), 1.84x latency at batch 16, and 1.72x the training H100-hours to get there. The sample strip is uncurated: seed 9 shows the single-token G3 checkerboard tail artifact, which we diagnose on slide 10.
Likely objection: "the UniPC gain is just a solver" — correct, and we applied it to R0 too; the gap persists.
Sources: reports/dct_causal/efficiency/phase2_verdict.json, bench.json, bench_r0.json; reports/dct_causal/efficiency/baseline.json.

slides.title: Why order image generation by frequency?
slides.notes:
Purpose: position the factorization against the two standard ones.
Joint diffusion (DCTdiff, EDM...) denoises everything at a shared noise level; spectral coarse-to-fine behaviour is emergent (DCTdiff even argues diffusion is implicitly spectral AR). Spatial AR generates pixels/patches serially. Ours makes frequency the explicit causal axis: four groups of block-DCT coefficients, each generated as an entire 8x8 spatial field, conditioned on all lower groups.
The bottom row is real data, not model output: decoding a real FFHQ-64 image with only G0 gives the 16x16 luma / 8x8 chroma block means; adding G1 gives edges; G2 and G3 add detail.
Important honesty point: we do not assume frequency causality is superior. The interesting questions are whether it helps quality, conditional diversity, training efficiency or sampling efficiency. The rest of the deck answers each separately.
Source: reports/dct_causal/efficiency real10k cache; lsb/dct_causal/ffhq64_eff.py lowpass convention.

slides.title: A1: one axial transformer, causal across frequency
slides.notes:
Purpose: the exact model, from the code (libs/axial_freqk.py, AxialFreqK with rep dct4x4k9; config ffhq64_exp.py:a1_d256).
Representation: DCTdiff's own FFHQ representation ported to 64x64: YCbCr 4:2:0, 4x4 block DCT, first 9 zig-zag coefficients; one token = an 8x8-pixel area = 4 luma blocks + Cb + Cr, 6 blocks x 9 = 54 channels, 64 tokens. Groups are u+v of the zig-zag position: G0 = DC; G1 = (0,1),(1,0); G2 = (2,0),(1,1),(0,2); G3 = (0,3),(1,2),(2,1). Note (3,0) is not in the 9 retained coefficients, so G3 is not orientation-symmetric.
Trunk: the state is [batch, slots, 1+64 tokens, 256]. Each block does split-head axial attention with one shared QKV: 3 spatial heads attend densely over the 65 tokens within a slot (no spatial order), 1 frequency head attends across slots at the same spatial position under the mask on the right. Training packs clean G0..G2 (teacher forcing) and noisy G0..G3 (independent t per stage) into one forward; noisy G_k sees clean G_<k and itself only, so all four conditionals are trained per example.
Parameter sharing: all 13 blocks, positional and time embeddings are shared across stages; only the per-stage input/output linear adapters and the stage embedding are stage-specific.
Sampling: an outer loop over k; for each k an inner UniPC ODE (20/10/8/8 calls) integrates the noisy field while the clean prefix's per-layer frequency-head keys/values are computed once and cached (exact: clean slots never depend on noisy slots or on t).
Do not confuse: the outer autoregression is over frequency groups; the inner process is a standard diffusion ODE over one spatial field.

slides.title: Next-frequency generation, stage by stage (real samples)
slides.notes:
Purpose: make "next-frequency prediction" concrete with genuine samples.
Left: six uncurated samples (std seeds 0-5) from A1 at 250k with the UniPC [20,10,8,8] sampler. Row 1 shows only G0 - the DC of every 4x4 block, i.e. a 16x16 luma / 8x8 chroma mosaic: it already fixes identity-level layout, pose, colour. G1 adds first-order gradients (edges), G2 and G3 add texture and sharpness.
Right: what each group contributes on its own (contrast-stretched; G1-G3 have very different energies). The bar chart is the measured noise influence: re-sampling only G0's noise changes 98% of pixel variance and 99% of the Inception-feature change of a fully independent draw; G1 noise moves 31% of the features but under 3% of pixels; G3 only 12%.
So G0 decides the layout almost completely. This is why a G0 error is so consequential, and why our efficient sampler gives G0 the most solver calls.
Source: decoded from /dev/shm/nadavo_dct/eff/runs/j20_10_8_8/s0_coef.pt; phase1_verdict.json noise_pixel_share / noise_feature_share.

slides.title: Three references isolate what frequency causality does
slides.notes:
Purpose: make clear which comparison answers which question.
R0 is DCTdiff's official FFHQ-128 "small" U-ViT recipe ported to 64x64, run in our environment with our evaluator (44.2M parameters). It reproduces the authors' released CIFAR checkpoint (FID-10K 8.50 vs 8.54), so we trust the port.
A0 and A1 are the same 11.09M-parameter axial network. A0 makes all four groups noisy at one shared t with bidirectional frequency attention: it is a joint diffusion model with our backbone. A1 adds the clean prefix slots, independent noise levels per stage, and the causal mask.
So A1 - A0 is the clean test of the factorization. A1 - R0 asks whether the whole package is competitive, but mixes backbone, capacity and token design.
Likely objection: A1 does 1.75x A0's training FLOPs per image (31.1 vs 17.8 GFLOP) because the clean prefix is re-encoded. We therefore report matched steps, matched H100-hours and matched FLOPs separately (slide 7).
Earlier designs (spatial-causal U-ViT - wrong axis; 256-token block-causal staging - 4.18x FLOPs; channel-lane causality - capacity confounded) are in appendix A5.

slides.title: CIFAR-10: causality looked nearly free, then plateaued
slides.notes:
Purpose: the first evidence, including the part that went against us.
On CIFAR-10 at D192, A1 looked almost free relative to its joint control (A1/A0 = 1.05 at 100k). With the wider D256 network trained to 250k, A0 kept improving (13.99 -> 10.98) while A1 flattened near 12.8, so A0/A1 went 0.95 -> 0.83: the causal penalty grows with training. The early comparison was misleading.
Single-axis screens (all 100k, pre-registered rules): width is the only clear win; more spectral stages in the same 4x4 DCT (K3 -> K7) gave 0.95x FID at 2.06x compute; the full-image DCT with 8 bands overfit badly - each early global band has ~12 degrees of freedom per image so the next band becomes a lookup (train loss falls, held-out loss rises); a persistent Gaussian context G_-1 and stage-noise jitter were neutral.
The sample rows show the single-token checkerboard already on CIFAR (frog, car).
Do not compare these FIDs with FFHQ numbers: different dataset, representation (2x2 DCT, 3 groups) and reference statistics.
Source: reports/dct_causal/scaling/summary.json; narrative SCALING_SUMMARY and D256_NOTE.

slides.title: FFHQ-64: frequency AR beats its joint control
slides.kicker: FFHQ-64  ·  EQUAL TRAINING BUDGET (3.34 H100-h EACH)  ·  EULER [100]×K
slides.notes:
Purpose: the result that made the project interesting again.
Protocol (PREREG_FFHQ64.md): jpeg-ar's q90 FFHQ-64 (all 70k images), NVlabs EDM Inception FID against the q90 reference; every arm gets 3.34 H100-hours, R0's measured time to 250k. Throughput probes set A1 to 146k steps and A0 to 174k. Final checkpoints scored with FID-50K and precision/recall at n=50k; all with the original matched Euler sampler (100 calls per stage).
Result: R0 12.66, A1 15.08 (1.19x R0), A0 18.49. On FFHQ the frequency-AR model beats its joint control at matched steps, matched H100-hours and recall - the reverse of CIFAR. Per training FLOP it is roughly a tie, because A1 does 1.75x A0's FLOPs per image; A1's hour advantage partly comes from better GPU utilisation.
BandJoint (our older design, 122.5M parameters, different architecture and training budget) is shown only as a historical point under the same evaluator: A1 is 1.41x better with 11x fewer parameters.
Caveats to say out loud: one training seed per arm; all arms short of maturity; this is not proof that low-to-high frequency order is universally better (slide 11 has the reverse-order control).

slides.title: More training brought A1 close to R0, at higher cost
slides.notes:
Purpose: what more training buys, and why we stopped.
The compute-matched A1 (146k) was resumed from its full state (weights, EMA, AdamW moments, scheduler) with everything frozen except the step count (PREREG_A1_FFHQ64_MATURITY.md). The pre-registered 200k gate passed; the 200k->250k leg was a weak improvement (-0.31 FID-10K). The FID-50K rule then triggered: 13.69 at 250k, 1.08x R0's 12.66.
That is quality proximity, not efficiency: it took 5.77 H100-hours (1.72x R0) and 1.77x R0's training FLOPs, and recall stays below R0 (.347 vs .375). The G3 tail outlier rate also grows with training (2.9% -> 3.6%).
Panel (a) mixes nothing: all FID-10K, all Euler. Panel (b) is FID-50K only at the checkpoints where it was evaluated. FID-10K is systematically ~1.2-1.3 higher than FID-50K here, which is why we never place them on one axis.
Important framing: this was our conclusion before solver optimization - the next slide changes the sampling picture, not the training picture.

slides.title: UniPC: 400 → 46 evaluations, FID-50K 13.75 → 9.46
slides.kicker: SAMPLER  ·  SAME FROZEN A1 250k WEIGHTS, PAIRED NOISE
slides.notes:
Purpose: the largest single improvement, stated with its fairness control.
Phase 2 of the efficiency campaign kept A1's 250k weights frozen and only changed the sampler. The original Euler sampler (100 calls per stage, 400 serial calls) was both under-converged and badly allocated. Per-stage allocation curves showed G0 needs 15-20 UniPC calls (its errors amplify 3-4x into later bands) while G2/G3 tolerate 8. The winning joint schedule [20,10,8,8] = 46 calls gives FID-50K 9.46 vs 13.75 (paired seeds, -31%) and recall +0.064, at 8.0x lower batch-500 GPU-seconds and 9.3x lower batch-16 latency.
The fairness control is essential: the same UniPC applied to R0 gives FID-50K 8.68 at 15 calls (8.69 at 20). So A1/R0 stays ~1.09 and A1 remains 1.4-1.8x slower to sample. Distilling G2/G3 to 1-2 calls would save at most 12 of 46 calls and cannot close the serial-depth gap, so it was not run.
Likely objection: "you tuned A1's schedule more than R0's" - R0 was swept over UniPC 10/15/20/30/50, with 15 and 20 confirmed on a second seed set; both give FID-50K ~8.7.
Source: efficiency/phase2_verdict.json, bench.json, bench_r0.json, runs.json (f50_*).

slides.title: Where A1 fails: later groups lose conditional diversity
slides.notes:
Purpose: locate the remaining deficit, carefully distinguishing interventions from attribution.
(1) G0 is the most influential group (its noise controls 98% of pixel variance and perturbations amplify 3-4x downstream) but is adequately modelled: its PCA-64 coverage matches the real-vs-real reference and spread/skill is 0.99.
(2) The real-prefix oracle (an intervention): replacing G0 with the real image's coefficients drops FID-10K 14.92 -> 11.11; adding real G1 -> 7.31; G2 -> 4.13; all real -> 3.01 (the representation floor). Shares 32/32/27/9%. These are cumulative increments along one path, not additive causal attributions; and real prefixes are training images that are also in the FID reference.
(3) The deficit grows with frequency and is a diversity/scale problem: with a REAL prefix, G2/G3 already have spread/skill 0.83/0.81 and energy 0.90/0.88 (under-dispersed conditionals); with the model's own prefix the coverage gap widens to -0.13/-0.22 and energy to 0.84/0.71. The pre-registered rules make H1 (conditional variance under-estimation compounding through the chain) primary, H2 (spatial capacity) marginal; H3 (exposure bias) fails its rule.
(4) A zero-training probe that rescales each generated group about the data mean (alpha fitted on a separate calibration set) improves FID-10K 10.77 -> 10.50 and recall +0.015 - consistent with H1, and the motivation for the running candidate A.
(5) The tail artifact: one token's G3 coefficients explode when that token's own Gaussian noise has norm beyond ~3 sigma; the network under-predicts extreme input noise at t=1, and sigma/alpha amplifies it. It is visible in ~2-3% of images but costs nothing measurable in FID (truncating the noise tail changes FID by +0.05 on CIFAR).

slides.title: Only width helped clearly; finer serialization never did
slides.notes:
Purpose: one dashboard of the screens that changed our interpretation. Green = clear gain, grey = neutral, red = regression/negative, yellow = partial or important-but-provisional, cyan = gain that is not architectural.
CIFAR (100k, pre-registered helps <= 0.90x / hurts >= 1.10x): width is the only single-axis win. Finer spectral serialization buys little at large cost. The full-image DCT construction memorises (on 50k images, early global bands carry ~12 numbers per image). Refinement by the joint model recovers ~70% of the A1->A0 gap but never beats A0.
FFHQ (50k screens, canonical UniPC sampler, raw and EMA): shallower, more finely serialized (6 Euclidean rings) or less spatial (8x8 blocks, 16 tokens) variants all regress; editing earlier groups at inference through the frozen model's own loss does nothing beyond random edits.
Two FFHQ results matter most for the paper question:
- Reverse order (G3 -> G2 -> G1 -> G0, same parameters, verified leakage-free) is catastrophic at 100k: FID-10K 46.8 vs 13.7 with each direction's best sampler, 48.9 vs 17.4 at equal calls (UniPC-15 per stage). Low-to-high order matters for this architecture. Caveat: the prereg requires inspecting stagewise teacher-forced losses before attributing a >2x failure purely to ordering; that write-up is pending, and other orders (e.g. interleaved) were not tested.
- The variance probe is small but directional evidence for the H1 diagnosis.
Newest row (evaluated 11:22 IDT today): per-group data-std preconditioning, the training-time version of the variance probe. Paired over two seed sets it improves EMA FID-10K by 11.8% and recall by +0.07-0.08, but raw-weight FID is 0.6% worse (within seed noise), so under the strict pre-registered survivor rule it is borderline. Not yet adjudicated by the campaign - present it as early evidence only.
The UniPC row is included only so the dashboard is complete; it is a sampler, not an architecture change.

slides.title: Our present frontier: small and close, not cheaper
slides.kicker: WHERE WE STAND  ·  FFHQ-64, FID-50K, BEST VALIDATED SAMPLERS
slides.notes:
Purpose: the honest frontier, with three separately labelled axes.
A (quality vs sampling GPU-seconds, isolated H100 benchmark): R0 with UniPC-15 is better and cheaper than any A1 configuration. A1's UniPC point is 1.36x R0's GPU-seconds (and 1.84x its batch-16 latency).
B (quality vs training H100-hours): R0 reached 8.68 with 3.34 h; A1 needed 5.77 h for 9.46. We do not have a UniPC FID-50K for A1 at 146k (the equal-hours checkpoint), so we do not claim one.
C (quality vs parameters, marker area = recall): A1 and R0 are both on the frontier - neither dominates. This is the one axis where A1 wins: 11.1M vs 44.2M parameters.
I verified Pareto status only among the points plotted. A0 appears only with Euler because its UniPC result is FID-10K only (15.00, vs A1 at 250k 10.77 on the same protocol). BandJoint is a different architecture trained on A5000s; it appears only in the size plot and is clearly dominated.
Conclusion sentence is the requested one, and it is what the data support.

slides.title: Prior art: what we cannot claim to be new
slides.kicker: PRIOR ART  ·  ALL ENTRIES CHECKED AGAINST THE PAPER (APPENDIX A10)
slides.notes:
Purpose: an accurate novelty map, so we do not overclaim.
Categories: explicit coefficient AR (DCTransformer: quantized sparse DCT triples, one scalar per step; JPEG-LM: an LLM over JPEG bytes); joint diffusion in DCT space (DCTdiff - our R0 and our representation); groupwise sequential diffusion over frequency (GDM); frequency/scale-level AR with tokenizers (FAR-Yu with continuous latents and a per-token diffusion MLP; NFIG with frequency-guided residual VQ; SpectralAR with nested spectral tokens; VAR with scales); continuous-token AR with non-diffusion heads (GIVT GMM, JetFormer flow+GMM, MAR diffusion MLP); multi-scale conditional flows (Wavelet Flow).
What we cannot claim: frequency-ordered AR, per-stage diffusion over frequency groups, DCT diffusion, or the solver.
What might be defensible, if supported by controls: making frequency an explicit causal axis inside one axial network with an exact prefix cache, and generating each group as a jointly modelled spatial field (FAR-Yu and MAR use per-token heads; Nash is per-scalar). The reverse-order result and the measured per-band evaluation allocation are candidate findings, not yet mechanisms.
Missing: a written-up order mechanism, any frontier win against optimized DCTdiff, the F1 diffusion-free result, and a second dataset/resolution.
All rows were checked against the papers (links in appendix A10).

slides.title: Next experiments, and what each outcome would imply
slides.notes:
Purpose: what we will run, its status, and how outcomes map to claims.
A (order): completed as a 100k screen - reverse order is catastrophic, recall collapses to 0.055. Remaining: the pre-registered inspection of stagewise teacher-forced losses before we attribute the failure purely to order; an interleaved order would make the claim sharper.
B (diffusion-free head): the prior-art audit chose a conditional affine-coupling flow over each whole field (GMM-per-location discards within-field spatial dependence; MaskGIT needs quantization). All seven pre-training gates pass (round trip 1.3e-5, exact log-det, synthetic density gap 0.007 nats/dim, zero leakage, spatially coupled samples). The 50k pilot is queued, not run.
C (coefficient-plane K=9): authorized only. Our own evidence (CIFAR K7 neutral at 2x compute; FFHQ 6-ring K6 -42% raw FID) makes a positive outcome unlikely; if run, generator family is held fixed so granularity is the only change.
D (late-group dispersion): candidate A (per-stage data-std preconditioning, motivated by the H1 diagnosis and the variance probe) finished its 50k pilot this morning. Paired FID-10K (mean of std and 31M seeds) vs the A1 50k control: EMA 28.81 -> 25.41 (-11.8%), raw 26.80 -> 26.96 (+0.6%, within ~0.2 seed noise); recall +0.077 (EMA) / +0.070 (raw). Strictly, the FID clause fails on raw and the recall clause needs 'FID not worse', which raw misses by 0.16 - borderline. The campaign has not adjudicated it; I report it as early and unadjudicated. Candidate B (depthwise 3x3 mixer with an equal-parameter 1x1 control) started training at ~11:22 IDT.
Survivor rule (pre-registered): >=5% better paired FID-10K in raw AND EMA at 50k, or +0.02 recall without FID loss, with serial calls unchanged and <=10% per-call latency growth.

slides.title: What is the actual paper contribution?
slides.notes:
Purpose: invite a decision, not applause.
Strongest claim we can defend today: on FFHQ-64, with the backbone held fixed, explicit causal frequency generation beats joint generation at equal compute, and the reverse order is catastrophic - so the order is not arbitrary for this model. Practically, A1 matches DCTdiff to within 9% FID with a quarter of the parameters.
Main threat: FAR (Yu et al. 2025) already does next-frequency AR with a diffusion head on continuous tokens; GDM sequentially diffuses frequency groups; Nash et al. did low-to-high DCT AR. Our distinctions are real but are design combinations.
Missing: anything that beats optimized DCTdiff on training or latency, a written-up mechanism for why order matters, a second dataset/resolution, and the diffusion-free head.
Questions for Shai: (1) is frequency causality a distinct inductive bias or just a schedule; (2) what is the simplest stochastic field generator that keeps diversity; (3) which single experiment would make the work both competitive and differentiated.

slides.title: DCT packing: 54 channels, 4 radial groups
slides.notes: Exact packing from the code. The zig-zag truncation at 9 coefficients means G3 contains (0,3),(1,2),(2,1) but not (3,0); this asymmetry is inherited from DCTdiff and is the reason the F2 coefficient-plane order needs an explicit tie-break convention.

slides.title: Attention masks and causality checks
slides.notes: The mask shown is generated by the same rule as libs/axial_freq.slot_mask. The verification JSON stores the actual mask used in a traced forward, and the Jacobian tests are numerical, not by construction.

slides.title: Samplers: equations and evaluation accounting
slides.notes: Solver curves: UniPC beats DPM-Solver++(2M) and Euler for A1 at every budget; A1 FID rises with more uniform calls (UniPC-10 better than UniPC-50), i.e. a mildly over-dispersed fine solve trades precision for recall. R0 is flat from 15 calls on. The allocation figure is the evidence for giving G0 the most calls.

slides.notes: If asked why q90: the BandJoint campaign trained on q90-decoded images, and to compare against its 21.32 winner we kept its protocol. The official-reference FID is reported separately because it includes the codec floor.
